Role Summary The Project Manager – Capital Projects (Tailem Bend) is responsible for the delivery of the Tailem Bend project within Firmus’ South Australian capital projects portfolio. Design, cost and schedule changes are identified, assessed and recommended by this role, and authorised by the Senior Project Manager. The Project Manager is responsible for ensuring no change proceeds without that authorisation, and that approved changes are implemented, recorded and reflected in the project cost report and programme. Day to day, the role runs the project on the ground — directing consultants, contractors and vendors, controlling the programme and cost, maintaining safety and quality standards, and coordinating the planning, design, procurement, construction, fit-out, commissioning and deployment activities required to hand over a complete and operable facility. The role sits within the Capital Projects Team, which forms part of the Development Division under the Chief Development Officer. Prepare the project material required for gateway and investment approvals, including scope, cost plan, programme and risk, for review by the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects. Progress planning approvals, authority conditions, utility and network connections and enabling works in line with the approved programme. Run the day-to-day site delivery, including site supervision, coordination of trades and resolution of on-site issues. Programme and Cost Control Own and maintain the project programme, protecting critical path, interface dates and key milestones. Manage the project budget, including commitments, invoicing, variations, contingency drawdown and forecast to completion, with support from project controls. Produce accurate, timely project reporting on progress, cost, risk, safety and readiness for the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects. Identify risks, delays and cost exposures early, propose mitigation, and escalate promptly rather than after impact. Maintain complete and current project records, registers and documentation throughout delivery. Design and Change Management Coordinate design development with consultants to ensure the design meets the approved brief, is buildable and is delivered to cost and programme. Identify, assess and document every design, cost and schedule change, including its scope, cost, programme and risk impact. Submit all changes to the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects for authorisation — no change is to proceed on site without it. Implement approved changes and ensure they are reflected in the drawings, cost report, programme and project records. Manage requests for information, technical queries and design clarifications through to closure. Procurement, Consultants and Contractors Support procurement strategy and packaging for the project with the supply chain and procurement functions, including long-lead equipment and specialist trades. Manage the day-to-day performance of consultants, head contractors, construction managers, subcontractors and vendors engaged on the project. Administer contracts, including scope definition, variations, claims, progress claims and payment recommendations, close-out and final account. Hold delivery partners to the project programme and to the required cost, quality and safety standards. Safety, Quality and Compliance Ensure work health and safety requirements are understood and met by all parties on site, and that safety performance is actively managed rather than assumed. Ensure the works are delivered to the specified quality standards, with inspection and test plans, hold points and defect management applied. Ensure compliance with permit and approval conditions, environmental requirements and applicable codes and standards. Report incidents, near misses and non-conformances promptly and see corrective actions through to closure. Stakeholder and Authority Engagement Act as the Firmus representative on site, maintaining working relationships with the council, planning authority, network and utility providers, neighbours and the local community. Coordinate with internal functions — development and planning, design and engineering, project controls, energy and operations — to keep project delivery aligned with business requirements. Support the Senior Project Manager in customer engagement relating to the project through delivery, commissioning and handover. Commissioning, Deployment and Handover Coordinate commissioning, acceptance testing and witnessing through to a complete and operable facility. Confirm site readiness, environmental conditions and access ahead of equipment delivery, installation and deployment. Meet the handover readiness criteria set for the region, covering safety, quality, testing and documentation. Compile and transfer handover documentation — as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, asset registers, spares and operator training. Manage defects, close-out and the transition of responsibility to the operations team. Design, cost and schedule changes are identified early, properly assessed, authorised before they proceed, and reflected in the cost report and programme. Risks, delays and cost exposures are escalated ahead of impact, with practical mitigation proposed rather than problems simply reported. Safety and quality standards are met on site, with incidents, non-conformances and defects managed through to closure. Consultants, contractors and vendors perform to programme, cost and quality, with contracts properly administered and closed out.
